notes: CONFLICT FOR REVIEW, source-side fix required: the launch policy pairs LING with native ETH (pool.pairedCurrency is the zero address; admission refuses an ERC-20 paired currency, so IMD cannot be written here), but the accepted source fixes the token's rewardCurrency to IMD (0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7) when block.chainid == 1 (Swarmlings._chooseRewardCurrency) and SwarmlingsHook copies it into its immutable reward in its constructor. On Ethereum mainnet afterInitialize therefore never records an ETH / LING pool as launchPool: no 1.25% holder fee, no snipe tax, no JIT guard, no modules or slices run on the pool this manifest describes, distribute() reverts NotLaunched, and the first IMD / LING pool at fee 12500 that anyone later initializes with this hook becomes launchPool instead, at any tick spacing and price. The hook never reverts, so the deployer's simulation succeeds and the pool opens trading with only its 1.25% LP fee. The resolution is in the source, not in this manifest: _chooseRewardCurrency must return address(0) on chain id 1 (the hook's reward, minDistribute, README and docs then follow the native pairing the test suite already covers as the Native pairing), and the approved workflow, which says paired with IMD, must be re-approved for the ETH pairing. Until one of these happens this launch must not deploy. Contracts as accepted: Swarmlings is a DN404 token with a zero-argument constructor that deploys its NFT contract (SwarmlingsMirror) and mints exactly 1e27 LING (18 decimals) to msg.sender with skipNFT set; every whole 300,000 LING held by a wallet is one Swarmling NFT, 3,333 at most, minted and burned automatically; contracts skip NFTs unless they opt in, so the factory, PoolManager and distributor never hold any. The token and NFT contract have no admin, proxy, pause, mint after construction or fee on transfer; owner() returns DEV (0x92cef4823119f3332a85a39023eeba01a06890c4) only as the marketplace collection editor and has no power in the contracts. SwarmlingsHook's constructor takes (IPoolManager manager, address token), written as $poolManager and $token; it has no owner, factory or launch-number parameter. It declares all 14 hook flags in getHookPermissions and calls Hooks.validateHookPermissions in its constructor, so its address must have its low 14 bits set (0x3FFF); the deployer must mine the salt for that. beforeInitialize and afterInitialize are restricted to the PoolManager and return their selectors; beforeInitialize never rejects a pool, so the 12500 LP fee tier is accepted. afterInitialize records the first reward-currency / LING pool at static LP fee 12500 (LAUNCH_LP_FEE) as launchPool, at any tick spacing. Fee slices and modules can be changed only by SwarmlingsCouncil, a constant (COUNCIL, 0x4d0b3507d80f678d9e658fd5482ca6a96636a032) already deployed on mainnet and owned by DEV; the total hook fee is capped at 5% with the holders' 1.25% as a fixed floor, and no module can block a sell or a liquidity removal. At launch there are no slices and no modules. distribute(), syncEth(), syncToken(), addRewards() and a sink's poke() are open to anyone; claim(), claimEth() and claimToken() pay only the caller; claimDev() pays only DEV its half of the ETH creator fees (5% ERC-2981 on NFT sales to the token, half to holders). The hook holds no LING at launch and no contract here is allocated any supply. Art comes from the immutable renderer at 0x8d79e6677fa6e52190b39096f8496628811d8281 (constant RENDERER, deployed separately, not part of this launch). initialPrice is written as the launch facts give it; the deployer derives the opening price from the policy's opening market cap and the token's address.
